en: Heating an aerosol spray can increases the gas pressure inside, which can cause the metal container to explode dangerously.
Crushed activated charcoal filters dirty water by trapping impurities in its porous solid structure, providing a simple way to purify drinking water.
Mixing liquid bleach with ammonia-based cleaners creates toxic chloramine gas, so you must never combine these two common household cleaning solutions.
Applying a cold ice pack to a swollen sprain absorbs heat from the skin, reducing inflammation and numbing the pain.
Electrical wires are coated in rubber or plastic because these solid materials are insulators that prevent dangerous electric shocks.
A deeply rusted food can has a compromised metal seal that can let deadly botulism bacteria enter, so discard severely rusty cans.
You must shake liquid antibiotic suspensions before drinking them to evenly distribute the solid medicine particles settled at the bottom of the bottle.
Touching solid dry ice causes severe frostbite because its extremely cold temperature rapidly absorbs heat from your skin as it sublimates into carbon dioxide gas.
Mixing baking soda and vinegar creates a fizzy chemical reaction that safely cleans grout without using harsh, toxic commercial bathroom chemicals.
Heating cooking oil past its smoke point releases flammable vapors that can easily catch fire if exposed to an open stove flame.
Sweating cools your body down because the liquid water on your skin absorbs body heat to evaporate into a gas.
Oil and water form a separated mixture, which is why you must use soap to emulsify and wash grease off your dirty hands.
